title: Rollini, Bix and the three-trombone battle at Small's Paradise
summary: Waters was most struck by Rollini's bass saxophone and Bix, and recalls a battle of Miff Mole, Jack Teagarden and Jimmy Harrison at Small's, which Harrison won. He later got a bass saxophone in California.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: And the one who knocked me out the most as a saxophone player, see - I didn't hear any tenor players at that period that knocked me out more than Coleman, you understand what I mean, I didn't hear any - but that guy on the bass, Rollini, on the bass saxophone, every note he made was great. And naturally, naturally Bix knocked me out. And Miff Mole, I have a reason to say Miff Mole knocked me out, because I've heard a battle of three trombones right at Small's Paradise - Miff Mole, Jack Teagarden, and -

No, no, Jimmy Harrison, see what I mean? And that was the greatest thing I ever heard in my life, you know. We gave Jimmy Harrison the edge because he was, had more of this - Miff Mole had the technique, and so did Jack. Jack had a little bit more blues feeling than Miff Mole, but Jimmy had more than either one of them, of that thing

that we were talkin' about, that the Negro kind of excelled, particularly at that period. The Negro didn't excel at harmony and tone, they didn't excel - rather, they didn't play as well as the white boys, music - that's why the bands used to sound so great, you know. They were in tune, they had - where the white musicians didn't excel, solos. Then, I mean - not now, I mean 'cause guys kind of blow you out if you don't watch what (laughs). But I mean, at that period, you see, that's where, what I listened to, Goofus - not that I would base in their style, from any of 'em. Because I listened to Bix - if I was a trumpet player most likely I would prefer to play like Louis Armstrong, see. But if I was, I was a bass horn player, I didn't have a bass saxophone in Boston - no, that wasn't in Boston, I wasn't in Boston - but I did turn out later gettin' a bass saxophone in Los Angeles when I out there. That was later, you know, see.
I had my own band out in San Diego.
And that's a little bit further down the road.
Yeah, that's a little further, that's way down. See, but when I got this bass saxophone, the first person I thought of was Andre Rollini -
Because I preferred, that was my inspiration if I'm gonna play bass, which I didn't play often.
